is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for the knock-down resistance (kdr) gene mutations (Abstract, Page 1; Methods, Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports that 'The kdr PCR assay of 192 of the samples (148 survivors (DDT: 67; deltamethrin: 17; permethrin: 64: and 44 susceptible ones) however, did not reveal any kdr mutations in the mosquitoes' (Results, Page 4). This provides a count of 192 mosquitoes genotyped, all of which were wild-type (SS).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from the Kassena-Nankana district in northern Ghana (Abstract, Page 1; Methods, Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study reporting original field collection, bioassay, and molecular data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is localized to the Kassena-Nankana district (KND) and Navrongo in northern Ghana (Methods, Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected during two periods: November 2006 to April 2007 and July to October 2007 (Discussion, Page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study appears to be an independent investigation by the Navrongo Health Research Centre and does not mention being part of a larger multi-country consortium or previously published dataset.

supplement.evidence: All relevant genotype and bioassay data are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study assessed insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus in the Kassena-Nankana district of Ghana. WHO tube bioassays were performed for permethrin, deltamethrin, cyfluthrin, lambdacyhalothrin, and DDT. Molecular analysis (PCR) was conducted on 192 An. gambiae mosquitoes (including 148 bioassay survivors and 44 susceptible individuals) to detect kdr mutations. No kdr mutations were found in any of the samples tested, and all An. gambiae were identified as the M molecular form (An. coluzzii).
